items.q: Circumcorneal injection with cells and flare in the anterior chamber defines which diagnosis?
items.exp: Cells and protein leak mark intraocular inflammation with pain and photophobia; conjunctivitis keeps the chamber optically empty with discharge instead. Steroid and mydriatic therapy follows grading.
r: Incorrect. Dry eye burns without cells.
items.kp: Cells swimming inside: uveitis, not pink eye.

items.q: Large mutton fat keratic precipitates with Koeppe and Busacca nodules indicate which type?
items.exp: Macrophage rich granulomas dot endothelium greasily with iris granulomas; sarcoid, tuberculosis and sympathetic ophthalmia lead differentials needing chest and infective workup.
items.kp: Greasy big precipitates plus iris nodules: granulomatous.

items.q: Unilateral alternating acute anterior uveitis with back stiffness in a young man most suggests what?
items.exp: Alternating attacks with sacroiliitis, enthesitis or urethritis flag B27 disease; rheumatology co manages with NSAIDs and biologics while eyes get topical steroids. Bilateral granulomatous disease instead seeks sarcoid.
r: Incorrect. Behcet adds mouth and genital ulcers.
Incorrect. Herpes raises pressure with atrophy.
items.kp: Each eye in turn plus stiff back: B27.

items.q: Why are cycloplegic mydriatics mandatory in anterior uveitis?
o: Prevent posterior synechiae and relieve ciliary spasm pain
items.exp: Atropine or homatropine pulls iris from lens preventing seclusio and angle closure while paralysing the painful ciliary body; steroids alone leave adhesions forming. Dark glasses ease the dilated photophobia.
items.kp: Dilate uveitis or iris glues to lens.

items.q: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis is distinguished by which triad plus course?
o: Heterochromia with stellate precipitates, cataract and glaucoma but no synechiae, chronic unilateral
items.exp: Low grade chronicity without adhesions confuses with quiet eyes; cataract surgery and glaucoma management dominate while steroids barely help. Rubella and CMV associations are studied.
items.kp: Different coloured irises, quiet chronic cells: Fuchs.

items.q: Recurrent unilateral marked pressure spikes with mild anterior chamber cells is which entity?
items.exp: Trabeculitis blocks outflow episodically with halos and mild inflammation settling between attacks; aqueous suppressants with brief steroids abort crises while herpetic testing excludes mimics.
r: Incorrect. POAG is bilateral and painless.
items.kp: Pressure storms with whisper of cells: Posner Schlossman.

items.q: Irregular pupil with 360 degree posterior synechiae and rising pressure after missed uveitis treatment is what?
o: Seclusio pupillae with iris bombe and secondary angle closure
items.exp: Iris bombe balloons forward blocking trabeculum; urgent steroids with mydriatics and pressure lowering precede laser iridotomy once inflammation cools. Prevention beats this emergency.
r: Incorrect. Shape is irregular and fixed.
items.kp: Iris glued all round, ballooning forward: bombe.

items.q: Painful red eye with hypopyon and vitritis three days after cataract surgery is which emergency?
o: Acute postoperative endophthalmitis needing intravitreal antibiotics and vitrectomy
items.exp: Bacterial seeding (coagulase negative staph, streptococci) ferments inside with lid swelling and vision crash; vitreous tap with vancomycin and ceftazidime plus vitrectomy for severe cases saves eyes. Steroids alone blind.
r: Incorrect. Pain and vitritis exceed routine.
items.kp: Postoperative pus inside eye: tap and inject.

items.q: Sympathetic ophthalmia threatens which eye after penetrating injury and needs what?
o: Fellow uninjured eye with granulomatous panuveitis; urgent immunosuppression with injury repair
items.exp: Exposed uveal antigens sensitise systemically, inflaming the sympathising eye weeks later with mutton fat precipitates and Dalen Fuchs nodules; high dose steroids and steroid sparing agents preserve bilateral vision.
r: Incorrect. Fellow eye is the victim.
Correct. Spare eye inflames, suppress immunity.
items.kp: One eye pierced, other eye inflames weeks later: sympathise fast.

items.q: Chronic silent bilateral anterior uveitis with band keratopathy in a girl with arthritis is typical of what?
o: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis associated uveitis needing screening
items.exp: Oligoarticular JIA girls develop asymptomatic chamber cells scarring into cataract, glaucoma and band calcium; slit lamp screening every few months catches disease before synechiae. Pain absence delays presentation.
r: Incorrect. B27 aches acutely in adults.
Correct. JIA silent uveitis, screen regularly.
items.kp: Arthritic girl, quiet eyes, band calcium: screen JIA.
